subject: Technical validation & local SDK pilot plan for BeaconHealth integration
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@beaconhealth.org>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@beaconhealth.org>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: local SDK pilot scope & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete pilot plan so we can move to a short technical validation next week.

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: evaluate search + clinical note summarization in a sandbox; verify relevancy for clinician queries and runtime/latency for a 1–2k user pilot.
- Desired features to test: embeddings-based search, reranker for top-K relevancy, structured output for downstream EHR tool calling, and local SDK behavior for offline testing.
- Security constraints: PHI cannot leave Beacon-controlled environments during later stages; initial validation can use de-identified data or synthetic records.

Proposed local SDK pilot (2 weeks):
1) Week 0: provisioning — Redwood sandbox account, API key + ephemeral credentials, and shared quickstart docs (attached).
2) Week 1: local SDK runbook — run Python/TypeScript quickstarts against synthetic dataset; verify embeddings + reranker outputs and latency.
3) Week 2: end-to-end tool calling demo — structured output from model triggers a simulated EHR write (no real PHI).

Key technical asks for Beacon:
- Provide a small de-identified sample (~500 notes) or allow us to run on synthetic sample we supply.
- Confirm whether you prefer API key-based sandbox or a VPC/private deployment for the pilot.

Deliverables from Redwood:
- SDK quickstart PDF (attached) + local-env-checklist.md (attached)
- Example Python and TypeScript snippets for auth, embeddings, and structured output
- Short meeting (30m) for engineering deep-dive to lock config and security guardrails

Next steps / Proposed times for deep-dive: Tue or Wed next week 10–12 PT. Please confirm preferred slot and whether you want the sandbox set up with API keys or a VPC test environment.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart-v1.2.pdf (quickstart guide, snippets)
- local-env-checklist.md (local setup checklist)

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@beaconhealth.org>

Subject: Re: Post-call: local SDK pilot scope & next steps

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A few clarifying points from our side before we schedule the deep-dive:

1) Security / compliance: our Security team will need SOC 2 evidence and an explanation of where tokens are stored when running the SDK locally. Can you include a short note on how credentials are handled and whether we can run entirely offline with synthetic data?

2) Data residency: for pilot it's OK to use de-identified data in Redwood-hosted sandbox (US only), but long-term we may need a Private deployment in our VPC.

3) Embeddings/reranker: can you share which models you recommend for clinical notes (embedding dimension, expected token counts) and a sample reranker config? Also: do you provide reranker as a managed module or is it a pattern using embeddings + re-ranker model?

4) Local testing: we want minimal steps for engineers to run locally without sending PHI. Please include an explicit example of generating embeddings and running a local nearest-neighbor search with the SDK.

We can do Tue 11am PT for the deep-dive.

Best,
Sarah
Director, Clinical Apps | BeaconHealth
sarah.kim@beaconhealth.org

Subject: Re: Post-call: local SDK pilot scope & next steps — technical plan + snippets

Hi Sarah / Tom — Vivek from Redwood engineering here. Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise technical validation plan plus concrete local SDK snippets. I'll also attach a short checklist (local-env-checklist.md) and the quickstart PDF.

Security / credentials model (local):
- Sandbox option: API_KEY stored in an env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY). All local calls hit Redwood-hosted sandbox endpoints over TLS. No PHI required for initial pilot — use synthetic data.
- VPC/Private option: we provide a Private deployment package; credentials can be issued short-lived and stored in your KMS/HSM. For an on-prem pilot we can run the inference runtime inside your VPC with no egress.

SOC2 and evidence: we will share SOC2 Type II report and a short one-pager describing our token storage and telemetry. I'll request the SOC2 link from security (expect within 24–48h).

Model recommendations (initial pilot):
- Embeddings: use rwd-embed-clinical-v1 (512d) for note-level search. Good tradeoff for clinical semantics and cost.
- Reranker: pattern is embeddings + lightweight reranker model (rwd-ranker-small). We host the reranker as part of our managed serving stack; you call the reranker post-retrieval to rescore top-50 candidates.

Local SDK quickstart (Python):
- install: pip install redwood-sdk
- set key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"REDACTED_SANDBOX_KEY\"
- embeddings example:
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client()
  texts = [\"Note: patient presents with chest pain...\", \"Follow-up: BP elevated...\"]
  emb = c.embeddings.create(model=\"rwd-embed-clinical-v1\", input=texts)
  # store emb vectors locally and run faiss/annoy for nearest neighbor search

- rerank example:
  # after retrieval send topN ids back to reranker
  rerank = c.rerank.create(model=\"rwd-ranker-small\", queries=[{\"query\": \"chest pain\"}], candidates=emb_candidates)

Local SDK quickstart (TypeScript):
- install: npm install @redwood-ai/sdk
- set key: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REDACTED_SANDBOX_KEY
- embeddings example:
  import Redwood from '@redwood-ai/sdk'
  const client = new Redwood.Client()
  const texts = [\"Patient notes ...\"]
  const emb = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rwd-embed-clinical-v1', input: texts })

Routing & model selection notes:
- For pilot use hosted sandbox routing; endpoint selects GPU-backed serving nodes with quantized paths for embeddings.
- For production, routing policy can pin queries to Dedicated or Private deployments via the request header 'x-redwood-deploy-target'. We can provide sample middleware for your API gateway.

Structured output & tool calling:
- Our SDK supports function-like structured responses. Example: request a JSON schema for an EHR write and validate locally before triggering tool call.
- We recommend validating output with unit tests in CI that compare schema + confidence thresholds.

Local testing without PHI:
- Use synthetic dataset we provide (attached generator script).
- Run with REDWOOD_API_KEY pointing to sandbox. No PHI leaves your environment if you run against private deployment.

Attachments sent: redwood-sdk-quickstart-v1.2.pdf, local-env-checklist.md

Action items I will take by Mon: share SOC2 link and a sandbox API key for your test account. Vanessa: can you open a HubSpot task and assign a CS engineer?

If Tuesday 11am PT works, I will bring an engineer to walk through the snippets and run a live local run.

Regards,
